title: Chat interactions
purpose: Code-oriented candidate models for chat selection, composition, generation, message relationships and branches. Only stated UI surfaces have static capture support.

evidence_policy.observed: The saved HTML establishes selected UI regions and controls, not that a particular transition took place.
evidence_policy.candidate: State/event edges describe possible contracts for software authors. Every transition requires future verification; never treat it as a recovered ChatGPT protocol.
evidence_policy.data_protection: This public graph contains no chat text, user identifiers, actual conversation IDs, storage keys, request paths, payload examples or authentication data.

surfaces.label: Sidebar navigation
surfaces.description: Captured side region with two nested navigation regions. Whether each control selects a chat was not traced.

surfaces.label: Composer form
surfaces.description: Captured form with three buttons and four file inputs; handler ownership unknown.

surfaces.label: Textbox role
surfaces.description: A textbox role occurs in the saved document. Its association with the form was not demonstrated.

surfaces.label: Dialog
surfaces.description: A role=dialog region exists; opening, closing and focus behavior were not observed.

entities.label: Conversation
entities.description: Abstract conversation root with a local opaque reference. Not a claim about actual site storage fields.

entities.label: Message
entities.description: A possible node in a message graph. Content is deliberately not modeled in public examples.

entities.label: Branch selection
entities.description: Candidate model for alternative message paths. No branch-switching action was verified.

entities.label: Draft
entities.description: Local conceptual editing state. No stored text or attachment metadata is included.

entities.label: Response operation
entities.description: Possible response lifecycle used only to organize future experiments.

transitions.verify: In an authorized controlled session, select a non-sensitive test conversation and compare selected UI and route state before/after.
Compare before/after selection in a disposable test session; do not record identifiers or message text.
Test whether an explicit UI action clears selection; may be unsupported.
Record only generic editor state changes after synthetic typing; avoid recording content.
Observe generic editor change events without logging text.

effects: one logical request attempt may begin
transitions.verify: Submit harmless synthetic content under explicit permission and correlate UI state with a sanitized request event without endpoints or payloads.
Observe timing of first UI response update; log only timestamps and generic event category.
Observe final UI status in a disposable test conversation without content capture.
Only if a safe, naturally occurring error can be observed; do not induce unsafe failures.
Observe safe error state without storing content or network secrets.
Verify stop-control visibility, response status and event timing in an authorized test.
Verify whether a retry control exists and whether it creates a new attempt; absence is allowed.
Type synthetic content after a completed response and record general UI state.
Confirm whether reset is a real distinct action or simply a return to idle.

branch_model.description: Alternative response branches, edits, and regenerations should be modeled as graph structure only if later evidence confirms their identity and selection semantics.
required_observations: Does editing create a new message node or mutate an existing one?
Can more than one assistant response share a parent?
Does regeneration create a new attempt, new message, or both?
Do URLs or persisted state encode branch selection?

open_questions.question: What stable and ephemeral identities are needed to track a conversation without exposing actual account IDs?
open_questions.next_evidence: Synthetic opaque identifiers derived inside a local research harness; verify only equality/continuity properties.

open_questions.question: What order do selection, submission, streaming and completion UI events follow?
open_questions.next_evidence: An explicitly authorized controlled test with event types, timestamps and redacted correlation keys.

open_questions.question: Which state survives refresh, reload, tab switch or browser restart?
open_questions.next_evidence: Observe state continuity only; never publish storage keys or values.

open_questions.question: Which generic route state maps to selected conversation or active branch?
open_questions.next_evidence: Record only presence/shape changes; keep all real routes and identifiers private.

open_questions.question: How do edits, regeneration and alternate message paths actually affect the conversation graph?
open_questions.next_evidence: Use disposable synthetic conversations and record structural relationships only.

open_questions.question: Which request/stream event categories correspond to an action?
open_questions.next_evidence: Correlate abstract request and response events while removing payloads, tokens, endpoints and headers.

limitations: No live chat interactions were observed in the supplied ZIP.
Transition edges here are hypotheses for implementing a state-graph client, not recovered product behavior.
Observed UI surfaces do not establish exact React component, listener, endpoint or store ownership.
Private conversations and account identifiers are excluded from all public research.
